{{Short description|Pair of functions in combinatorics}}
In [[mathematics]], specifically [[combinatorics]], a '''Wilf–Zeilberger pair''', or '''WZ pair''', is a pair of functions that can be used to certify certain combinatorial [[identity (mathematics)|identities]]. WZ pairs are named after [[Herbert S. Wilf]] and [[Doron Zeilberger]], and are instrumental in the evaluation of many sums involving [[binomial coefficient]]s, [[factorial]]s, and in general any [[hypergeometric series]].  A function's WZ counterpart may be used to find an equivalent and much simpler sum.  Although finding WZ pairs by hand is impractical in most cases, [[Gosper's algorithm]] provides a method to find a function's WZ counterpart, and can be implemented in a [[computer algebra system|symbolic manipulation program]].

==Definition==
Two functions '''''F''''' and '''''G''''' form a WZ pair [[if and only if]] the following two conditions hold:

: <math>F(n+1,k)-F(n,k) = G(n,k+1)-G(n,k),</math> 
: <math>\lim_{M \to \pm\infty}G(n,M) = 0. </math>

== Properties ==
From the definition it follows that

: <math>\sum_{k=-\infty}^\infty [F(n+1,k)-F(n,k)] = 0</math>

because the function '''''G''''' [[telescoping series|telescopes]]:

:<math>\begin{align} \sum_{k=-\infty}^\infty [F(n+1,k)-F(n,k)] 
& {} = \lim_{M \to \infty} \sum_{k=-M}^M[F(n+1,k)-F(n,k)] \\
& {} = \lim_{M \to \infty} \sum_{k=-M}^M [G(n,k+1)-G(n,k)] \\
& {} = \lim_{M \to \infty} [G(n,M+1)-G(n,-M)] \\
& {} = 0-0 \\
& {} = 0.
\end{align}
</math>

Therefore,

: <math>\sum_{k=-\infty}^\infty F(n+1,k) = \sum_{k=-\infty}^\infty F(n,k), </math>

that is

: <math>\sum_{k=-\infty}^\infty F(n,k) = \text{const}.</math>

The constant does not depend on '''''n'''''. Its value can be found by substituting '''''n = n''<sub>0</sub>''' for a particular '''''n''<sub>0</sub>'''.

If '''''F''''' and '''''G''''' form a WZ pair, then they satisfy the relation

: <math> G(n,k) = R(n,k) F(n,k-1),</math>

where <math>R(n,k)</math> is a [[rational function]] of '''''n''''' and '''''k''''' and is called the ''WZ proof certificate''.

== Example ==
A Wilf–Zeilberger pair can be used to verify the identity

: <math>\sum_{k=0}^\infty (-1)^k {n \choose k} {2k \choose k} 4^{n-k} = {2n \choose n}. </math>

Divide the identity by its right-hand side:

: <math>\sum_{k=0}^\infty \frac{(-1)^k {n \choose k} {2k \choose k} 4^{n-k}}{{2n \choose n}} = 1. </math>

Use the proof certificate

: <math>R(n,k)=\frac{2k-1}{2n+1}</math>

to verify that the left-hand side does not depend on '''''n''''', where

:<math>\begin{align} 
F(n,k)&=\frac{(-1)^k {n \choose k} {2k \choose k} 4^{n-k}}{{2n \choose n}}, \\
G(n,k)&=R(n,k)F(n,k-1).
\end{align} </math>

Now '''''F''''' and '''''G''''' form a Wilf–Zeilberger pair.

To prove that the constant in the right-hand side of the identity is 1, substitute '''''n'' = 0,''' for instance.
